MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  NOVEMBER 13, 2018

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order by
MAYOR HUFF at 7:04 p.m. in the Council Chamber at Rolling Hills City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes
Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

MAYOR HUFF led the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None.

City Staff Present: City Manager, Douglas R. Prichard
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Planning Director David Wahba
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  A PROCLAMATION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES DECLARING NOVEMBER 24, 2018 AS SMALL BUSINESS SATURDAY

  MAYOR HUFF presented a proclamation declaring the November 24, 2018, the Saturday
  after Thanksgiving, as Small Business Saturday.

CONSENT CALENDAR

  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of
  the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by
  a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual consideration will be voted on
  separately.)

MAYOR HUFF stated that staff has requested that Item 5F be tabled for consideration at the
next meeting of the CITY COUNCIL. Hearing no objection, she so ordered.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
NOVEMBER 13, 2018
 MAYOR HUFF also commented regarding Item 5G that subsequent to the lengthy discussion at
the last meeting it was determined that the policy presented at the October 23 meeting did not
reflect the COUNCIL’S previous direction so it is before the COUNCIL again for affirmation.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS A-G AS
  PRESENTED BELOW.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF OCTOBER 23, 2018

  APPROVED AS PRESENTED.

C.  PENINSULA HOLIDAY PARADE SUBCOMMITTEE MINUTES OF OCTOBER 22, 2018

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

D.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS –OCTOBER AND NOVEMBER 2018

  APPROVED WARRANTS 60706 THROUGH 60757 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $447,805.63; AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 100118 THROUGH 101518;
  60280 (VOID); 60565 THROUGH 60567; 60610 THROUGH 60629; 60675
  THROUGH 60692 IN THE AMOUNT OF $253,603.95 FOR A GRAND TOTAL
  AMOUNT OF $701,409.58.

E.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 5, 2018

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING FOR THE FUNDING OF TABER GROVE
  DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION COSTS

  TABLED

G.  CITY PROPERTY AND FACILITY NAMING POLICY

  REAFFIRMED THE CITY PROPERTY AND FACILITY NAMING POLICY AS
  ADOPTED ON APRIL 24, 2018.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
NOVEMBER 13, 2018
 PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Korey Bradbury of Cal-Water provided an update on the progress of the Palos Verdes Peninsula
water reliability construction project and responded to COUNCIL’S inquiries regarding the project
related to the entryway at Montecillo and the paving/pavement markings.

A.  SCE WILDFIRE MITIGATION AND GRID RESILIENCY

  There were no representatives from SCE present to make the presentation.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE.

NEW BUSINESS

A.  MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING – ONSITE WASTEWATER TREATMENT
  SYSTEMS

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the Memorandum of Understanding
  (MOU) between Los Angeles County Department of Public Health (LACDPH) and the City
  of Rolling Hills Estates for the regulation of onsite wastewater treatment systems (OWTS)
  within the City subject to final review and approval by the City Attorney

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)
  Kathleen McGowan, McGowan Consulting provided a brief overview of the background
  and history of septic system regulations in Los Angeles County and the requirement for
  adopting the MOU.

  Discussion ensued concerning the number of properties in the City that are currently
  using a septic system and the options for connecting those properties to the County sewer
  system. Assistant City Manager Grammer commented that staff is in discussions with the
  Marloma Neighborhood about the process of forming a sewer assessment district and
  staff will be bringing the matter before the COUNCIL in the coming months for
  consideration.

  COUNCILMEMBER  ZERUNYAN  moved,  seconded  by  COUNCILMEMBER
  ZUCKERMAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE MEMORANDUM OF
  UNDERSTANDING (MOU) BETWEEN LOS ANGELES COUNTY DEPARTMENT
  OF PUBLIC HEALTH (LACDPH) AND THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES
  FOR THE REGULATION OF ONSITE WASTEWATER TREATMENT SYSTEMS
  (OWTS) WITHIN THE CITY SUBJECT TO FINAL REVIEW AND APPROVAL BY
  THE CITY ATTORNEY.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
NOVEMBER 13, 2018
 B.  AMENDED AND RESTATED NATURE CENTER SERVICES AGREEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the Amended and Restated Nature
  Center Services Agreement with Palos Verdes Peninsula Land Conservancy for Nature
  Center contract Naturalist services through June 30, 2020.

  Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report (as per agenda material.) He
  noted that that the cost includes an increase of 15% to cover the Land Conservancy’s
  costs associated with operating the Nature Center.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN regarding the justification for the
  increase, Adrienne Mohan, Conservation Director, PVPLC stated that the increase is to
  bridge the $15,000 gap in the cost to provide the services they are currently providing.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE AMENDED AND RESTATED
  NATURE CENTER SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH PALOS VERDES
  PENINSULA LAND CONSERVANCY FOR NATURE CENTER CONTRACT
  NATURALIST SERVICES THROUGH JUNE 30, 2020.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

OLD BUSINESS

NONE.

CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

NONE.

CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS:

  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to provide information and
  reports to other Members of the City Council and/or the public on any issues or activities of currently
  active Council Committees, ad hoc committees, regional or state-wide governmental associations,
  special districts and/or joint powers authorities and their various committees on which Members of
  the City Council might serve or have an interest, which are not otherwise agendized.

COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN reported that the CCA Board of Directors will be meeting this
Thursday to set rates for the coming year.

MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL reminded COUNCIL that the SCAG Economic Summit will be
held on Thursday, December 6, 2018.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
NOVEMBER 13, 2018
 MAYOR HUFF reported that Supervisor Hahn attended the recent SBCCOG Steering
Committee meeting to urge support for Alignment Option C3 as an interim solution related to LA
Metro’s Green Line expansion. She also reported on dinners/events attended by COUNCIL
including RPV’s 45th Anniversary dinner and Mayor Garcetti’s dinner during the National League
of Cities event in Los Angeles.

MAYOR HUFF commented that that the CITY provided shelter for several horses evacuated
from Malibu as a result of hte Woolsey Fire.

COUNICLMEMBER ZUCKERMAN noted that Martin Gombert from PV Transit was instrumental
helping secure bus transprotation for many evacuees as well.

MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS:

  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to request information on
  currently pending projects and/or issues of public concern, direct that an item be agendized for future
  consideration and/or make announcements of interest to the public.

A.  AUTHORIZATION TO ATTEND THE CALIFORNIA CONTRACT  CITIES  2019
  SACRAMENTO LEGISLATIVE TOUR – JANUARY 7-9, 2019

  COUNCILMEMBER  ZERUNYAN  moved,  seconded  by  COUNCILMEMBER
  ZUCKERMAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL AUTHORIZE ALL COUNCILMEMBERS TO ATTEND
  THE CALIFORNIA CONTRACT CITIES 2019 SACRAMENTO LEGISLATIVE TOUR
  – JANUARY 7-9, 2019

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

OTHER MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS:

MAYOR COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN inquired as to the status of the Torrance Airport
stormwater project in light of the fact the Measure M passed. Assistant City Manager Grammer
commented that at this time, it does not appear that it will be feasible for the Peninsula Cities to
partiaicpate.

At 7:49 p.m. MAYOR HUFF adjourned the open session portion of the City Council meeting in
memory of the victims of the last week’s mass shooting at Borderline Bar and Grill in Thousand
Oaks and victims of the devastating wildfires in Northern and Southern California. The COUNCIL
recessed into closed session to discuss the matter listed below.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
NOVEMBER 13, 2018
 CLOSED SESSION

A.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Government Code §54957
  Title: City Manager (Quarterly Evaluation)

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION

ADJOURNMENT

At 9:50 p.m. MAYOR HUFF formally adjourned the City Council meeting. An adjourned meeting
of the City Council will be held on Tuesday, November 27, 2018 at 5:00 p.m. at City Hall, 4045
Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California for the purpose of conducting
Commission/Committee interviews. The next regular meeting of the City council will be held on
Tuesday, November 27, 2018 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 4045 Palos
Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Heidi Luce  Douglas R. Prichard
City Clerk  City Manager

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
NOVEMBER 13, 2018
